title: Reject a transaction whose card number is not in the card cross-reference file
summary: The program looks up each daily transaction's card number in the card cross-reference file. If the card is not found, the transaction fails with reason 100 'INVALID CARD NUMBER FOUND', the account lookup and account checks are skipped, and the transaction is rejected instead of posted.

given.text: Before each daily transaction is validated, the failure reason is set to 0 and the failure description is set to spaces.
The lookup key for the cross-reference file is the transaction's 16-character card number.

when.text: No cross-reference record exists for that card number (keyed read returns INVALID KEY).

then.text: The failure reason is set to 100 and the description to 'INVALID CARD NUMBER FOUND'.
The account lookup and account checks run only when the failure reason is still 0, so they are skipped after a card lookup failure.
A transaction with a non-zero failure reason is not posted: the reject count goes up by 1 and a reject record is written. A transaction with reason 0 is posted.

title: Reject a transaction that would take the account over its credit limit
summary: When the account is found, the program computes a projected balance: current-cycle credits minus current-cycle debits plus the transaction amount. It stores this in a signed field with 9 integer digits and 2 decimals. If the credit limit is less than that value, the transaction fails with reason 102 'OVERLIMIT TRANSACTION'.

given.text: The account record was found for the cross-referenced account ID.
The projected balance is current-cycle credit minus current-cycle debit plus the daily transaction amount.

The projected balance is stored in a signed field with 9 integer digits and 2 decimals. The account cycle fields have 10 integer digits, so a result of 1,000,000,000 or more loses its high-order digit when stored (there is no ROUNDED or ON SIZE ERROR).

when.text: The account credit limit is less than the stored projected balance. A balance exactly equal to the limit passes.

then.text: The failure reason is set to 102 and the description to 'OVERLIMIT TRANSACTION'.

notes: The check uses only current-cycle credit and debit, not ACCT-CURR-BAL.
The account's active status (ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS) does not appear to be checked during validation.

judge.reason: The READ of ACCOUNT-FILE has a NOT INVALID KEY branch, which is the record-found path the rule's logic sits in.
Lines 403-405 compute WS-TEMP-BAL = ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT - ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT + DALYTRAN-AMT, exactly as stated.
WS-TEMP-BAL is declared PIC S9(09)V99 and the cycle fields are S9(10)V99, so standard COBOL truncation drops high-order digits of results of 1,000,000,000 or more when no ON SIZE ERROR is coded.
The IF passes (CONTINUE) when ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT >= WS-TEMP-BAL, so the ELSE fires only when the limit is less than the balance, and equality passes.
The ELSE branch moves 102 to WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON and 'OVERLIMIT TRANSACTION' to WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON-DESC.

title: Reject a transaction that originated after the account expiration date (overrides over-limit)
summary: When the account is found, the program compares the account expiration date, as text, with the first 10 characters of the transaction's origination timestamp. If the expiration date is earlier, the transaction fails with reason 103 'TRANSACTION RECEIVED AFTER ACCT EXPIRATION'. This check runs after the credit-limit check whatever that check found, so it overwrites reason 102 when both fail.

given.text: The account record was found for the cross-referenced account ID.
The account expiration date is a 10-character text field, and the transaction origination timestamp is a 26-character text field.

when.text: The expiration date is less than the first 10 characters of the origination timestamp. The comparison is character by character, and an equal date passes.

then.text: The failure reason is set to 103 and the description to 'TRANSACTION RECEIVED AFTER ACCT EXPIRATION'.
The expiration check runs after the credit-limit check, whatever that check found. If both fail, reason 103 and its description overwrite reason 102.

notes: The character comparison gives a correct date order only if both values use the same YYYY-MM-DD layout.

judge.reason: The cited READ with its NOT INVALID KEY branch shows that the following logic runs only when the account record is found by XREF-ACCT-ID.
The copybooks declare ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE as PIC X(10) and DALYTRAN-ORIG-TS as PIC X(26).

The expiration IF follows the credit-limit IF unconditionally within NOT INVALID KEY, so when both fail, the MOVEs of 103 and its description overwrite the earlier 102 values.

title: Route each daily transaction to posting or to the reject file, and set return code 4 when anything is rejected
summary: Each daily transaction record is validated. If the failure reason code is still 0, the transaction is posted. Otherwise the reject count goes up by one and a reject record is written, made of the full 350-byte daily record followed by an 80-byte trailer holding the reason code and its description. When the run ends, the program prints the processed and rejected counts and sets return code 4 if at least one transaction was rejected.

given.text: For every daily transaction record read, the processed-transaction count goes up by 1. The failure reason code is reset to 0 and its description to spaces before validation runs.

A reject record is 430 bytes. It holds a 350-byte copy of the transaction data followed by an 80-byte validation trailer. The trailer is a 4-digit unsigned reason code followed by a 76-character reason description.

when.text: After validation, the failure reason code decides what happens: 0 means the transaction is posted, and any other value means it is rejected.

then.text: If the reason code is 0, the transaction is posted: the transaction-category balance is updated, then the account record, then the transaction file is written. The reject branch (reject count and reject record) is skipped for that transaction.
If the reason code is not 0, the reject count goes up by 1 and one reject record is written for that transaction.
The reject record holds the whole daily transaction record unchanged, followed by the trailer containing the current reason code and description. It is written to the daily rejects file.
At the end of the run, the program prints the processed count and the rejected count with fixed labels.
If at least one transaction was rejected, the program ends with return code 4. Otherwise the return code is left unchanged.

notes: The posting step 2800-UPDATE-ACCOUNT-REC can set reason code 109 ('ACCOUNT RECORD NOT FOUND') if the account rewrite fails. That happens after the post-or-reject decision, so the transaction is still written to the transaction file, no reject record is produced and the reject count does not change.

The reason code only decides the routing; the main flow itself never examines specific code values (100, 101, 102, 103). If a transaction both exceeds the credit limit and arrives after the account expiry date, the expiry code 103 overwrites 102 in the trailer.
Any I/O error on the rejects file (status other than 00) abends the program, so no return code is set for that run.

title: Transaction category balance is created or increased by the posted amount
summary: For each transaction that passed validation, the program looks up the category balance record by account ID, transaction type and category code. If no record exists, it writes a new one whose balance is the transaction amount. If the record exists, it adds the amount to the balance and rewrites the record.

given.text: A daily transaction is posted only when validation left the fail reason at 0.
The category balance key is built from the account ID found in the card cross-reference, the daily transaction type code and the daily transaction category code.
The category balance is held as a signed number with 9 integer digits and 2 decimals. The transaction amount has the same size.

when.text: The category balance record is read by key. If no record exists for the key, the create flag is set to 'Y'. Otherwise it stays 'N'.

then.text: When the create flag is 'Y', a new category balance record is written. It is initialised, its account ID, type code and category code are set from the cross-reference and daily transaction, and its balance is set to 0 plus the transaction amount.
Otherwise the transaction amount, with its sign, is added to the existing category balance and the record is rewritten.

notes: The ADD has no ON SIZE ERROR clause. If the balance overflows S9(9)V99, the high-order digits are dropped silently.
A read status other than '00' or '23', or a failed write or rewrite, ends the program with an abend. That is plumbing.

Order of posting (lines 440-442): the category balance is updated first, then the account record, then the transaction record is written. This was moved out of the clauses because those lines name only paragraphs and contain no data names or literals the checker can verify.

title: Account balance and cycle credit/debit are updated by the posted amount
summary: The posted amount is added to the account's current balance. A zero or positive amount is also added to the current-cycle credit. A negative amount is added, still negative, to the current-cycle debit. The account record is then rewritten.

given.text: The account record was read during validation, using the account ID from the card cross-reference.
The current balance, cycle credit and cycle debit are each signed numbers with 10 integer digits and 2 decimals.

when.text: A transaction passed validation (its fail reason is still 0), so it is posted, and posting runs the account update.

then.text: The transaction amount, with its sign, is added to the account's current balance.
If the amount is zero or positive, it is added to the current-cycle credit.
If the amount is negative, it is added, still negative, to the current-cycle debit. The debit total therefore becomes more negative.
The updated account record is rewritten to the account file.
If the rewrite fails with an invalid key, the fail reason is set to 109 with the text 'ACCOUNT RECORD NOT FOUND'. Posting still goes on to write the transaction record.

notes: Reason 109 is set after the reject decision in the main loop has already been made. It appears to have no effect: no reject record is written and the reject count is not increased.
The ADDs have no ON SIZE ERROR clause. If a field overflows S9(10)V99, the high-order digits are dropped silently.

Not covered here: 2000-POST-TRANSACTION copies the daily transaction fields into TRAN-RECORD, stamps TRAN-PROC-TS with the current time in YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.hh0000 format, and 2900 writes that record to TRANSACT-FILE.

title: Category balances are processed in account groups (control break on account ID)
summary: Category balance records are read one by one in key order. When the account ID changes, the account loaded before is written back with its interest (except on the very first record), the interest total is reset to zero, and the new account and its card cross-reference are read. Every record, including the first of a group, then goes on to rate lookup, and interest is only calculated when the rate is not zero.

given.text: Category balance records are read one at a time, in key order, from the category balance file, which is indexed and read sequentially. The record key starts with the account ID, so all categories for one account come in together.
At program start the last-seen account number is spaces and the first-time flag is 'Y'.

when.text: A category balance record is read and its account ID differs from the last-seen account number.

then.text: If this is not the first account group, 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT runs for the account loaded before: it adds the accumulated interest total to the account's current balance, sets the current-cycle credit and debit to 0, and rewrites the account record. On the first group the first-time flag is only set to 'N'.
The interest total is reset to 0 and the last-seen account number is set to the new account ID.
The account record for the new account ID is read by key from the account file into ACCOUNT-RECORD.
The card cross-reference for the account is read through the account-ID alternate key. Its card number is the one later copied into the card number of each interest transaction.

For every category balance record, whether or not the account changed, the rate lookup key is built from the account's group ID and the record's category code and type code, and the interest rate is looked up.
Interest is calculated (and the fee step run) only when the interest rate found is not zero. Records with a zero rate add nothing to the account's interest total.

notes: The program relies on the category balance file arriving in account order. If the same account appeared in two separate runs of records, its account record would be updated twice, each time with only part of the interest.

WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM is PIC X(11) and is compared with the numeric display field TRANCAT-ACCT-ID 9(11). Its starting value of spaces never matches a real account ID, so the first record always triggers a break.
WS-RECORD-COUNT is counted up for each record read, but within this unit it is only kept in working storage.

title: Account balance update with accumulated interest at account break
summary: When an account group ends because the next record belongs to a different account, the account's interest total is added to its current balance, the current-cycle credit and debit are set to zero, and the account record is rewritten. Because of how the loop is written, the last account group in the file is never updated.

given.text: Each calculated monthly interest amount is added to an interest total for the account. The total holds 9 integer digits and 2 decimals, signed.

when.text: 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT runs when a record for a new account arrives and it is not the first account group.

then.text: The account's interest total is added to its current balance (signed, 10 integer digits and 2 decimals).
The account's current-cycle credit and current-cycle debit are both set to 0. This happens even when the interest total is zero.
The updated account record overwrites the existing account record in the account file.

When the read hits end of file, END-OF-FILE becomes 'Y' inside the iteration. The loop condition is tested before each pass, so the loop ends before the ELSE branch that would update the last account can run. The last account group's interest is therefore not added and that account record is not rewritten.

notes: The ELSE branch at line 220 looks meant to post the last account at end of file, but it cannot run because PERFORM UNTIL tests its condition before each pass. Interest transactions for the last account are still written to the transaction file, but its balance is not updated. A faithful port must copy this behaviour.
If the account read failed with INVALID KEY, the program abends because the status is not '00', so the update never runs against a missing account.

title: Interest rate lookup by account group, with fallback to the DEFAULT disclosure group
summary: For each category balance, the program looks up the interest rate in the disclosure group file using the account's group ID, transaction type code and transaction category code. If no record matches, it tries again with group ID 'DEFAULT' and the same type and category. Any other read failure stops the program. Interest and fees are calculated only when the rate found is not zero.

given.text: The disclosure group key is built from three parts in this order: the account's group ID (10 characters), the transaction type code (2 characters) and the transaction category code (4 digits).
The interest rate on the disclosure group record is a signed number with 4 integer digits and 2 decimal places.

when.text: The program reads the disclosure group file by that key into the disclosure group record.

then.text: If the read status is anything other than '00' (found) or '23' (not found), the program displays 'ERROR READING DISCLOSURE GROUP FILE' and abends.

If the record is not found (status '23'), the program replaces the group ID in the key with 'DEFAULT', padded with spaces to 10 characters. The type and category codes stay the same, and the program reads the default record.
If the DEFAULT record cannot be read (status not '00'), the program displays 'ERROR READING DEFAULT DISCLOSURE GROUP' and abends.
Interest and fees are calculated for the category balance only when the interest rate found is not zero. When the rate is zero, the balance is skipped.

judge.reason: Lines 210-212 move the account group ID, category code and type code into the key fields, and the FD layout at lines 78-81 orders the key as group ID X(10), type code X(02), category code 9(04).
DIS-INT-RATE is declared PIC S9(04)V99, a signed number with 4 integer digits and 2 implied decimal places.
Line 416 performs READ DISCGRP-FILE INTO DIS-GROUP-RECORD, a keyed read using the FD key populated beforehand.
A status other than '00' or '23' sets APPL-RESULT to 12, so APPL-AOK is false, and the program then displays 'ERROR READING DISCLOSURE GROUP FILE' and performs 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM.

On status '23' the program moves 'DEFAULT' into the X(10) group-ID field (space-padded by MOVE semantics), leaves the other key parts untouched and performs 1200-A-GET-DEFAULT-INT-RATE, which reads DISCGRP-FILE.
In 1200-A-GET-DEFAULT-INT-RATE, any status other than '00' sets APPL-RESULT to 12, which leads to displaying 'ERROR READING DEFAULT DISCLOSURE GROUP' and performing the abend.
Lines 214-217 perform 1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST and 1400-COMPUTE-FEES only when DIS-INT-RATE NOT = 0, so a zero rate skips both calculations.

title: Monthly interest on a category balance
summary: For each transaction-category balance whose interest rate is not zero, monthly interest is the balance times the annual rate divided by 1200, truncated to 2 decimals. It is added to the account's running interest total, and one interest transaction is written.

given.text: Interest is computed only when the rate found for this category balance (DIS-INT-RATE) is not zero. A zero rate skips the computation, so no transaction is written for that balance.
The category balance is a signed amount with 9 integer digits and 2 decimals. The interest rate is a signed annual percentage with 4 integer digits and 2 decimals.
The running interest total is reset to 0 each time the account ID on the category balance record differs from the previous record's account ID.

when.text: Monthly interest is computed as (category balance x interest rate) / 1200.

then.text: The result is stored in a signed field with 9 integer digits and 2 decimals. ROUNDED is not used, so extra decimals are truncated toward zero.
The monthly interest is added to the account's running interest total, a signed field with 9 integer digits and 2 decimals.
Next, the interest-transaction paragraph runs and writes one transaction record (FD-TRANFILE-REC, built from TRAN-RECORD) to the transaction file for this category balance.

judge.reason: Lines 214-217 perform 1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST (and fees) only when DIS-INT-RATE NOT = 0, so a zero rate skips the computation; the claim that no transaction is then written follows because the write is performed from within 1300 (line 468).
TRAN-CAT-BAL is PIC S9(09)V99 and DIS-INT-RATE is PIC S9(04)V99, matching the stated signed formats; the 'annual percentage' reading is consistent with the /1200 monthly divisor.
Lines 194-201 set WS-TOTAL-INT to 0 whenever TRANCAT-ACCT-ID differs from WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM, which is then updated to the current account ID, so it holds the previous record's account.
Lines 464-465 compute WS-MONTHLY-INT = (TRAN-CAT-BAL * DIS-INT-RATE) / 1200.

Line 467 adds WS-MONTHLY-INT to WS-TOTAL-INT, which line 169 declares as PIC S9(09)V99.

title: Interest transaction record contents
summary: Each interest amount is written as a new record to the transaction file. The transaction ID is the run date parameter followed by a 6-digit sequence number. Type is 01, category is 05, source is System, and the description is 'Int. for a/c ' plus the account ID. The amount is the monthly interest, and both timestamps are set to the current time.

given.text: The transaction sequence counter (an unsigned 6-digit number) goes up by 1 before each interest transaction is built.

when.text: The transaction ID is the 10-character run date parameter followed by the 6-digit sequence counter (with leading zeros), 16 characters in total.

then.text: Type code is set to '01' and category code to '05'. The category code is a 4-digit numeric field, so it holds 0005. Source is set to 'System'.
The description is the text 'Int. for a/c ' followed by the 11-digit account ID.
The amount is the computed monthly interest. Merchant ID is set to 0, and merchant name, city and zip are set to spaces.
The card number is copied from the card cross-reference record found for the account.
Origination and processing timestamps both get the same current date and time, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.hh0000 (hundredths of a second followed by '0000').
The record is added as a new 350-byte record (a 16-byte ID plus 334 bytes of data) to the sequential transaction output file.

notes: The sequence counter starts at 0 and is not reset per account, so transaction IDs keep counting up across the whole run. It is a 6-digit field and would wrap after 999999 transactions.
STRING does not pad its target. Characters 25-100 of TRAN-DESC keep whatever the record held before (initially unset), and nothing clears them explicitly.
If the write fails, the program displays an error and abends (plumbing).

judge.reason: Line 474 adds 1 to WS-TRANID-SUFFIX before the record is built, and line 173 declares it PIC 9(06), an unsigned 6-digit number.

Lines 490-494 move WS-MONTHLY-INT to TRAN-AMT, 0 to the merchant ID, and spaces to the merchant name, city and zip.
